task.title: M9: Timeline scrub (play the treemap and graph through a commit range)
task.description:
Analyze every Nth commit (or one per week) across a range and let the user scrub the treemap and graph through time with a slider and play button. codeviz analyze gains --every <n> and --range <base>..<head> to produce the snapshot series (cached per SHA like any other), the snapshot index records the ordered series, and the UI adds a scrubber to the treemap and graph views. The requirement that makes this useful is layout stability: treemap tile positions and graph node positions must persist across adjacent snapshots so that motion means change rather than re-layout noise (treemap: fixed sort by path, not size; graph: seed fcose from the previous positions and only lay out new nodes). Export includes the series so a published site can play it.

Acceptance criteria:
- codeviz analyze --range v0.1.0..HEAD --every 10 analyzes the sampled commits in order and prints the count; already-cached SHAs are skipped.
- Scrubbing between adjacent snapshots keeps unchanged files in the same treemap region and unchanged graph nodes within a small displacement; new nodes fade in and removed nodes fade out.
- Play advances at an adjustable rate and can be paused; the hash records the current SHA so a position is linkable.
- Works on the static export; one test for the series sampling.
